decision.summary: The tenant reported a rotten-egg smell from the gas boiler and called it 'not urgent'. I treated it as a gas emergency. I sent evacuation and 0800 111 999 advice first, opened emergency job JOB-102, assigned HeatRight Ltd, told the landlord, and raised a P1 escalation.

answers.question: 1. What severity is this and why, given the tenant says it is 'not urgent'?
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell from a gas boiler is a suspected gas leak, whatever the tenant calls it. An 82-year-old guest is also in the flat. Policy treats a gas smell as an emergency.

answers.question: 2. What exactly do you tell the tenant right now, and in what order?
answers.answer: First, turn the boiler off if safe and don't use switches or flames. Second, open windows and get everyone out. Third, call 0800 111 999 from outside, or 999 if anyone is unwell. Then don't go back in until an engineer says it's safe, and message us once she is safe. The message also says an engineer is being sent.

answers.question: 3. Which actions do you take tonight (job, contractor, escalation, landlord)?
answers.answer: Sent the safety message (A1). Created emergency job JOB-102 (A2). Assigned HeatRight Ltd, the landlord's preferred Gas Safe contractor with out-of-hours cover (A3). Raised a P1 escalation, ESC-103 (A4). Emailed the landlord Ben (A5).

actions_claimed.description: Assigned HeatRight Ltd for emergency visit

conflicts: The tenant says 'not urgent' and asks for a visit tomorrow, but the symptoms indicate a gas emergency. I went with the symptoms.
The tenant asked for a late visit because of the elderly guest. Safety overrides that.
assumptions: The guest's age means extra risk, though the tenant record says vulnerable: false.
The smell is from the boiler, as reported, and not from elsewhere.

args.body: Hi Amelia, thanks for telling us. A rotten-egg smell from a boiler can be a gas leak, so please treat it as urgent tonight. Please: 1) Turn the boiler off if you can do so safely, and don't use any switches, flames or sockets near it. 2) Open windows and doors, and get everyone out of the flat, including your flatmate's mum. 3) Once outside, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24 hours). If anyone feels dizzy, sick or has a headache, call 999. Please don't go back in until the gas engineer says it's safe. We're sending a Gas Safe engineer and our team is being alerted now. Please message back once you're outside and safe.
